title: Record-intake scorer for the library-specialty dev fixture (reader-integration-0212 blockers 5-6)
body:
## Goal
Write `benchmark/scripts/score_record.py`, a record-intake scorer recommended in `benchmark/challenges/reader-integration-0212.md` `## Recommendation`. It reads one run-record JSON in the `benchmark/scripts/run_record.py` format, builds `submitted` with `run_record.score_answer`, scores correctness and grounding with `score.compute` against the `library-specialty` dev fixture, and prints outcome counts per frozen ID. Fidelity is reported as `not-applicable/unexecuted` when no reader response exists.
First step, before writing code: read `benchmark/scripts/score.py` lines 234-367 (`compute`) and confirm whether an absent reader response is accepted. If it is not and cannot be handled without changing score.py, report that as the blocker and stop (report, do not fix score.py).
Do not change any existing file: score.py, run_record.py, runner_contract.py, fixtures, `benchmark/results/` and every pinned file stay byte-identical. Do not import `src/`. No session can run LabVIEW; claim no LabVIEW behaviour and no quality result (native slots keep correctness `unverified`, `benchmark/challenges/README.md:8`). `benchmark_executed` stays false.
Expected gain: the next shaper reads the report line stating whether scorer and record formats compose (yes / no with file:line), so a future real answer record needs no new glue.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `benchmark/scripts/score_record.py` exists; `python3 -B -I benchmark/scripts/score_record.py --check` exits 0 without LABVIEW_ENVIRONMENT (use an in-memory or repository-only loader for the check; state in the docstring what the check does not cover)
- [ ] `--check` runs the synthetic record derived from `runner_contract.py` / `run_record.py` through the full path, and internally asserts that altering one claim answer changes the outcome (the check fails if it does not)
- [ ] The script writes nothing under `benchmark/results/` and imports nothing from `src/`
- [ ] No existing file changed; no `__pycache__` under `benchmark/`
- [ ] The report states: whether `compute` accepts an absent reader response (file:line), whether the formats compose, and any caveat

## Verification
`python3 -B -I benchmark/scripts/score_record.py --check`

## Context
- Source of the task: `benchmark/challenges/reader-integration-0212.md` (`## Existing`, `## Blockers` 5-6, `## Recommendation`).
- `score.py:234` `compute(source, denominators, inventory, submitted, probe, alignment, load_bytes)`; `score.py:618-631` `main`; `run_record.py:95-108` `score_answer`.
- Tool note: if the CLI answers "No such tool available: Read. Read is disabled for this session", that is a native-tool refusal, not a broker failure; propose the same operation again as a JSON action (orchestrator skill, Role tools, Policymaker #854). Grep is literal substring only.
- Do not check changes with `git status` (the worker directory is not a git repository). Check bytecode with `python3 -c "import pathlib; assert not list(pathlib.Path('benchmark').rglob('__pycache__'))"`. Run benchmark python with `python3 -B -I`.

## Budget
- Read: `benchmark/challenges/reader-integration-0212.md` whole; `benchmark/scripts/score.py` lines 1-60, 115-180, 234-367, 560-631 only; `benchmark/scripts/run_record.py` lines 1-20 and 90-130; `benchmark/scripts/runner_contract.py` lines 1-40 and the synthetic-record builder it names; `benchmark/challenges/library-specialty.json` by key (no whole read if over 300 lines).
- No whole large JSON files; short command output; report early if `compute` blocks the path.
